title: Fruitful service gives the life a path
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
summary: The shabad opens by calling service to the Lord fruitful and honorable. It travels through meeting the Guru, finding the Lord through the Shabad, and rejecting stubbornness as a path to discovery.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person who feels busy but inwardly aimless. Kept close, it reconnects usefulness, guidance, and purpose so the day is no longer just maintenance.
takeaway: Remember this: the path becomes visible when service turns fruitful.

lines.gurmukhi: ਹਰਿ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਸਫਲ ਹੈ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਪਾਵੈ ਥਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: har kee sevaa safal hai gurmukh paavai thai ||
lines.translation: Service to the Lord is fruitful; through it, the Gurmukh is honored and approved.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਸੁ ਹਰਿ ਭਾਵੈ ਤਿਸੁ ਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਸੋ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jis har bhaavai tis gur milai so har naam dhiaai ||
lines.translation: That person, with whom the Lord is pleased, meets with the Guru, and meditates on the Name of the Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਈਐ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਰਿ ਲਘਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur sabadhee har paieeaai har paar laghai ||
lines.translation: Through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, the Lord is found. The Lord carries us across.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨਹਠਿ ਕਿਨੈ ਨ ਪਾਇਓ ਪੁਛਹੁ ਵੇਦਾ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: manahaTh kinai na paio puchhahu vedhaa jai ||
lines.translation: Through stubborn-mindedness, none have found Him; go and consult the Vedas on this.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ਸੋ ਕਰੇ ਜਿਸੁ ਲਏ ਹਰਿ ਲਾਇ ॥੧੦॥
lines.transliteration: naanak har kee sevaa so kare jis le har lai ||10||
lines.translation: O Nanak, he alone serves the Lord, whom the Lord attaches to Himself. ||10||

structure: The shabad begins by giving service weight, fruit, and honor instead of treating it as leftover work.
From there it links guidance, Naam, and discovery through the Guru's Shabad.
The closing movement rests by stripping stubbornness of its authority and letting the Lord attach the servant.
